chapters.title_en: Our Earth in the Solar System
core_themes: Celestial bodies: Stars, Sun, Planets, Satellites, Asteroids, and Meteoroids.
Constellations (Ursa Major/Great Bear, Saptarishi) and the Pole Star (North Star).
The Solar System: The Sun as center, eight planets in order from Sun (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune).
Earth as a unique planet: Goldilocks zone, presence of water, air, and protective atmosphere.
The Moon: Earth's natural satellite, phases of the moon, absence of life.
Milky Way Galaxy (Akash Ganga) and the expanding Universe.
learning_outcomes: Differentiate between stars and planets.
Explain why Earth is called the Blue Planet and a unique planet.
Understand phases of the moon and distance scales in space.
Locate solar system planets and recognize asteroids between Mars and Jupiter.
summary_points: The Sun and celestial bodies revolving around it form the Solar System.
Earth is the third nearest planet to the Sun and the fifth largest planet.
Earth is called a unique planet because optimal temperature, liquid water, and life-supporting oxygen are present.
Light travels at $300,000\text{ km/s}$; sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
Asteroids orbit between Mars and Jupiter.
map_skills: Asteroid belt position between Mars and Jupiter

core_themes: The Globe as a true 3D miniature model of the Earth.
Axis, North Pole, and South Pole.
Equator ($0^\circ$) dividing Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

Parallels of Latitudes: Tropic of Cancer ($23\frac{1}{2}^\circ\text{ N}$), Tropic of Capricorn ($23\frac{1}{2}^\circ\text{ S}$), Arctic Circle ($66\frac{1}{2}^\circ\text{ N}$), Antarctic Circle ($66\frac{1}{2}^\circ\text{ S}$).
Three Heat Zones of the Earth: Torrid Zone, Temperate Zones, and Frigid Zones.
Meridians of Longitude, Prime Meridian ($0^\circ$) passing through Greenwich, Longitude and Local Time, Indian Standard Time (IST, $82^\circ 30'\text{ E}$).
International Date Line ($180^\circ$ Meridian).
learning_outcomes: Locate points on the globe using coordinate grid (latitude and longitude).
Explain differences between parallels of latitude and meridians of longitude.
Relate angle of sun rays with heat zones on Earth.
Calculate local time differences based on longitudes.
summary_points: Globe represents the true spherical shape (geoid) of the Earth tilted at $23\frac{1}{2}^\circ$.
All parallels of latitude decrease in size from the Equator to the poles.
All meridians of longitude are semicircles of equal length meeting at the poles.
Earth rotates $360^\circ$ in 24 hours, meaning $15^\circ$ per hour or $1^\circ$ every 4 minutes.
Indian Standard Time is based on the longitude of $82^\circ 30'\text{ E}$ passing through Mirzapur, which is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT.
map_skills: Equator, Tropics, and Polar circles on world outline

core_themes: Difference between a globe, map, sketch, and plan.
Types of Maps: Physical maps (relief features), Political maps (boundaries, cities, nations), Thematic maps (rainfall, roads, industries).

Three Components of Maps: Distance (Scale - small scale vs large scale maps), Direction (North Arrow, Cardinal directions N, S, E, W and intermediate directions NE, SE, SW, NW), Symbols (Conventional signs and international colors: blue for water bodies, brown for mountains, yellow for plateaus, green for plains).
Sketches (rough drawing without scale) and Plans (scaled drawing of small area like a room).
learning_outcomes: Identify types of maps and their appropriate uses.
Use map scale to calculate real ground distances.
Interpret conventional signs, symbols, and standard colors used in cartography.
Draw a sketch map of one's school or neighborhood showing landmarks.
summary_points: A map is a representation of Earth's surface or part of it drawn on a flat surface according to a scale.
A scale is the ratio between the distance on the map and the corresponding distance on the ground.
Large scale maps show small areas with high detail; small scale maps show continents or countries.
The North arrow helps orient directions; conventional symbols provide maximum information in minimum space.

core_themes: Major landforms of Andhra Pradesh: Mountains/Hills (Kondalu), Plateaus (Peethabhumulu), and Plains (Mydhanalu).
The Eastern Ghats in AP: Hill ranges including Nallamala, Veligonda, Palakonda, Erramala, and Seshachalam hills; highest peak Arma Konda ($1,680\text{ m}$) in Visakhapatnam district.
Plateau region of Rayalaseema: Deccan plateau extension, rocky terrain, black and red soils, dry climate, drought challenges.
Coastal Plains of Andhra Pradesh: Srikakulam to Nellore along the Bay of Bengal, fertile Krishna and Godavari deltas.
Major rivers flowing through AP: Godavari, Krishna, Penna, Vamsadhara, Nagavali.
Livelihoods, crops, irrigation tanks, borewells, and canal networks.
learning_outcomes: Identify the three major physiographic divisions of Andhra Pradesh.
Trace the courses of Krishna and Godavari rivers and their delta formations.
Compare agricultural practices and water availability between Coastal plains and Rayalaseema plateaus.
Locate major hill ranges and rivers on the outline map of Andhra Pradesh.
summary_points: Andhra Pradesh has three distinct landforms: Eastern Ghats, Rayalaseema plateau, and Coastal plains.
The Coastal plain extends along the Bay of Bengal coastline of about 974 km.
Krishna and Godavari deltas are known as the rice bowl of Andhra Pradesh due to fertile alluvial soils.
Rayalaseema plateau receives low rainfall and depends on tanks, borewells, and dryland crops like groundnut and millets.
map_skills: Rivers Godavari and Krishna delta in AP
Eastern Ghats hill ranges and Bay of Bengal coastline

core_themes: Hunter-gatherers of the Paleolithic Age (Old Stone Age): Hunting wild animals, gathering fruits, nuts, roots, and seeds.
Nomadic life and reasons for moving from place to place (seasonal fruits, movement of game animals, drying up of water sources).
Stone tool technology: Flint core tools, flake tools, and Microliths (Mesolithic).
Discovery and use of fire (cooking food, protection from wild beasts, light in caves). Rock art at Bhimbetka, Belum caves, and Kurnool caves.
Beginning of Agriculture and Pastoralism (Neolithic Age): Cultivation of barley, wheat, and rice; domestication of dog, sheep, goat, and cattle.
Invention of the wheel, pottery for cooking and grain storage, settled mud-brick huts (e.g., Mehrgarh, Burzahom), and Megalithic burial traditions.
learning_outcomes: Explain reasons why early humans lived a nomadic life.
Describe how the discovery of fire and invention of agriculture transformed human society.
Identify archaeological evidence of early humans in Andhra Pradesh (Kurnool caves, Nagarjunakonda).
Compare life of hunter-gatherers with settled agriculturalists.
summary_points: Early humans lived by hunting and food gathering for millions of years.
Traces of ash found in Kurnool caves in AP prove early use of fire by Paleolithic humans.
Neolithic humans settled in villages, cultivated crops, tamed animals, and made pottery on the potter's wheel.
Megaliths were large stone slabs placed over burial grounds by early iron age communities.
map_skills: Paleolithic and Neolithic sites in India: Kurnool caves, Bhimbetka, Mehrgarh, Burzahom

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What archaeological evidence found in Kurnool caves of Andhra Pradesh indicates that early humans used fire?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ లోని కర్నూలు గుహలలో లభించిన ఏ పురావస్తు ఆధారాలు ప్రాచీన మానవుడు నిప్పును ఉపయోగించాడని నిరూపిస్తున్నాయి?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Cite evidence of ash in Kurnool caves for discovery of fire.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read the paragraph on 'Invention of the Wheel' and explain how it revolutionized transport and craft making.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 'చక్రం కనిపెట్టడం' పాఠ్యభాగాన్ని చదివి, చక్రం రాకతో రవాణా మరియు కుండల తయారీలో ఎలాంటి విప్లవాత్మక మార్పులు వచ్చాయో వివరించండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Interpret the transformative impact of the wheel on human civilization.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, locate and mark the following prehistoric sites: (a) Bhimbetka, (b) Kurnool caves, (c) Mehrgarh, (d) Burzahom, (e) Hunsgi.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో క్రింది ప్రాచీన రాతియుగ ప్రదేశాలను గుర్తించండి: (a) భీమ్‌బేట్కా, (b) కర్నూలు గుహలు, (c) మెహర్‌గఢ్, (d) బుర్జాహోమ్, (e) హున్స్‌గి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Locate major Indian Paleolithic and Neolithic archaeological sites.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: How do prehistoric cave paintings in Bhimbetka and Belum show the artistic sensitivity and close relationship of early humans with wildlife?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భీమ్‌బేట్కా మరియు బేలుమ్ గుహలలోని రాతి చిత్రాలు ఆదిమ మానవుల కళాత్మక దృష్టిని, జంతువులతో వారికి గల అనుబంధాన్ని ఎలా తెలియజేస్తాయి?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Appreciate prehistoric rock art as evidence of early human creativity and nature harmony.

core_themes: The Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilisation (2500–1700 BCE): First urban civilisation in the Indian subcontinent.
Cities and Town Planning: Citadel (Upper town) and Lower town, baked bricks, grid iron street layout.
Unique architectural marvels: The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro, granaries of Harappa, dockyard of Lothal, water reservoirs at Dholavira.
Drainage system: Covered inspection drains running parallel to houses, soak pits.
Life in the city: Rulers, scribes, craftspersons; seals (Pashupati seal, Unicorn), steatite beads, bronze dancing girl, terracotta toys.
Trade with Mesopotamia (Dilmun, Magan, Meluhha).
Causes of decline: Deforestation, floods, shifting of river courses, drying up of Saraswati, over-utilization of resources.
learning_outcomes: Explain the remarkable features of town planning in Harappan cities.
Describe the construction and civic hygiene of the Indus drainage system and Great Bath.
Analyze Harappan crafts, seals, and long-distance trade.
Locate key Indus sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Lothal, Kalibangan, and Dholavira on the map.
summary_points: Harappa was discovered in 1921 in Punjab (now Pakistan), followed by Mohenjo-daro in Sindh.
Harappan cities were divided into two parts: elevated western citadel and lower eastern town.
Lothal in Gujarat had a tidal dockyard connected to the Sabarmati river for maritime trade.
Harappan script was pictographic and remains undeciphered to this day.
map_skills: Indus Valley Civilisation sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Lothal, Kalibangan, Dholavira

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Describe the main architectural features of the Great Bath found at Mohenjo-daro.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: మొహెంజొదారోలో బయల్పడిన మహా స్నానవాటిక (ది గ్రేట్ బాత్) యొక్క ముఖ్యమైన నిర్మాణ లక్షణాలను వివరించండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Describe the Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What made the Harappan drainage system unique and advanced compared to other ancient civilisations?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: హరప్పా నాగరికత కాలం నాటి భూగర్భ మురుగునీటి పారుదల వ్యవస్థ ఇతర ప్రాచీన నాగరికతల కంటే ఏ విధంగా విశిష్టమైనది?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Explain the advanced underground drainage system of Harappa.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read the section on 'The Dockyard at Lothal' and explain how overseas trade was carried out by Harappan merchants.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 'లోథాల్ లోని ఓడరేవు' భాగాన్ని చదివి, హరప్పా వర్తకులు విదేశీ వ్యాపారాన్ని ఏ విధంగా నిర్వహించేవారో వివరించండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Interpret overseas trade network of Harappans via Lothal dockyard.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Prepare a list of raw materials used by Harappans and the distant places from which they were obtained (Copper, Tin, Gold, Silver, Lapis Lazuli).
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: హరప్పా ప్రజలు ఉపయోగించిన ముడి పదార్థాలు మరియు అవి లభించిన సుదూర ప్రాంతాల వివరాలతో ఒక పట్టికను రూపొందించండి (రాగి, తగరం, బంగారం, వెండి, లాపిస్ లాజులీ).
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Tabulate Harappan raw materials and their geographic source locations.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, locate and label the major Harappan sites: (a) Harappa, (b) Mohenjo-daro, (c) Kalibangan, (d) Lothal, (e) Dholavira.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో ప్రధాన హరప్పా నగరాలను గుర్తించండి: (a) హరప్పా, (b) మొహెంజొదారో, (c) కాలిబంగన్, (d) లోథాల్, (e) ధోలవీర.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Locate major Indus Valley Civilisation archaeological sites on map.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What lessons on urban cleanliness, hygiene, and water conservation can modern smart cities learn from the Harappan civilization?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: పట్టణ పారిశుధ్యం, పరిశుభ్రత మరియు నీటి సంరక్షణ విషయాలలో నేటి ఆధునిక నగరాలు హరప్పా నాగరికత నుండి నేర్చుకోవలసిన పాఠాలు ఏమిటి?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Reflect on urban planning and civic hygiene lessons from Harappa for modern cities.

core_themes: From Janapadas to Mahajanapadas (around 600 BCE): 16 great territorial realms across the Indo-Gangetic plains.
Monarchies (Rajyas) vs Republics (Ganas or Sanghas).
Gana-Sanghas: Governance in Vajji confederacy, Lichchhavis, decision making through discussion in assembly halls (Santhagara).
Rise of Magadha as the most powerful Mahajanapada: Strategic geography (Ganga and Son rivers for transport and water), iron ore deposits in Rajgir for weapons, fertile plains, war elephants.
Rulers of Magadha: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Mahapadma Nanda.
Taxation system: Bhaga (1/6th of agricultural produce), taxes on craftspersons, traders, and herders; use of punch-marked coins.
Agricultural changes: Introduction of heavy iron plowshares, transplantation of paddy seedlings.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between a kingdom (monarchy) and a republic (gana-sangha).
Analyze the geographical and economic factors that led to the rise of Magadha.
Explain the ancient tax system and changes in agriculture during the Mahajanapada period.
Locate 16 Mahajanapadas on the outline map of India.
summary_points: Around 2500 years ago, some Janapadas became more important and were known as Mahajanapadas.
Most Mahajanapadas had a fortified capital city surrounded by huge brick or stone walls.
Magadha was ruled by powerful monarchs like Bimbisara and Ajatashatru with capitals at Rajagriha and later Pataliputra.
In Vajji (capital Vaishali), government was a Gana where decisions were taken in assemblies through debate.
map_skills: 16 Mahajanapadas: Magadha, Vajji, Kosala, Avanti, Gandhara, Vatsa

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What were the main differences between the system of government in Magadha and the Vajji Gana-sangha?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: మగధ రాజరికం మరియు వజ్జి గణతంత్ర రాజ్యాల పరిపాలనా విధానాల మధ్య గల ముఖ్యమైన తేడాలు ఏమిటి?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Contrast monarchy of Magadha with democratic assembly of Vajji.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain how the use of iron plowshares and paddy transplantation increased agricultural production around 600 BCE.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: క్రీ.పూ. 600 కాలంలో ఇనుప నాగలి కర్రుల వాడకం మరియు వరి నాట్ల పద్ధతి వ్యవసాయ దిగుబడిని ఏ విధంగా పెంచాయో వివరించండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Explain technological advances in agriculture: iron plowshare and paddy transplantation.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read the paragraph on 'Taxes in Mahajanapadas' and explain why kings needed regular taxes instead of voluntary gifts (Bali).
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 'మహాజనపదాలలో పన్నులు' భాగాన్ని చదివి, రాజులు స్వచ్ఛంద బహుమతులకు బదులుగా క్రమబద్ధమైన పన్నులను ఎందుకు వసూలు చేశారో వివరించండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Interpret the necessity of regular taxation for building forts and maintaining standing armies.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, locate and label the four major Mahajanapadas: (a) Magadha, (b) Vajji, (c) Kosala, (d) Avanti, and their capitals.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో నాలుగు ప్రధాన మహాజనపదాలను, వాటి రాజధానులను గుర్తించండి: (a) మగధ, (b) వజ్జి, (c) కోసల, (d) అవంతి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Locate major Mahajanapadas on ancient India outline map.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: In what ways was the Vajji Gana assembly similar to our modern democratic Gram Sabha or legislative assembly?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: వజ్జి గణ పరిషత్ చర్చా విధానం నేటి మన ప్రజాస్వామ్య గ్రామసభ లేదా శాసనసభలతో ఏ విధంగా సారూప్యతను కలిగి ఉంది?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Compare democratic participatory debate in Vajji assemblies with modern Gram Sabha.

core_themes: The Mauryan Empire (322–185 BCE): First pan-Indian empire founded by Chandragupta Maurya with assistance of Chanakya (Kautilya).
Kautilya's Arthashastra (principles of statecraft and economy) and Megasthenes' Indica (vivid accounts of Pataliputra).
Emperor Ashoka the Great: The Kalinga War (261 BCE), devastation, grief, and historic transformation from Digvijaya (military conquest) to Dhammavijaya (conquest by righteousness).
Ashoka's Dhamma: Moral ethical code (respect for parents, kindness to servants, religious tolerance, non-violence / Ahimsa).
Inscriptions on rocks and polished pillars in Prakrit language using Brahmi script.
Sarnath Lion Capital as the National Emblem of India.
Provincial administration: Pataliputra, Taxila, Ujjain, and Suvarnagiri.
learning_outcomes: Understand how an empire differs from a kingdom.
Explain the transformation of Ashoka after the Kalinga war.
Describe the core ethical teachings of Ashoka's Dhamma.
Identify the historical legacy of the Sarnath Lion Capital as India's National Emblem.
summary_points: An empire requires much larger resources, standing armies, and extensive bureaucratic networks than a kingdom.
Pataliputra was protected by massive wooden ramparts with 570 towers and 64 gates.
Ashoka is the only king in world history who gave up conquest after winning a war.
Ashoka appointed Dhamma Mahamattas to preach ethical conduct and inscribed rock edicts across the subcontinent.
map_skills: Ashokan inscription sites: Sarnath, Kalinga, Taxila, Amaravati, Yerragudi in AP

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What made Ashoka give up warfare after the Kalinga War? How did his policy of conquest change?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: కళింగ యుద్ధం తర్వాత అశోకుడు యుద్ధాన్ని ఎందుకు విరమించుకున్నాడు? అతని విజయ విధానంలో ఎలాంటి మార్పు వచ్చింది?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Explain Ashoka's renunciation of war after Kalinga.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What were the main problems that Ashoka tried to solve by introducing his Dhamma?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: అశోకుడు తన ధర్మం ద్వారా సమాజంలోని ఏ సమస్యలను పరిష్కరించడానికి ప్రయత్నించాడు?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Explain ethical problems addressed by Ashoka's Dhamma.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read Ashoka's edict on religious tolerance: 'One who honours his own sect and condemns other sects actually harms his own sect'. Interpret this statement in today's multi-religious society.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 'తన మతాన్ని గౌరవించి, ఇతరుల మతాలను కించపరిచేవాడు వాస్తవానికి తన మతానికే తీరని హాని చేస్తాడు' అనే అశోకుని శాసనాన్ని చదివి, నేటి బహుళ మతాల సమాజానికి దాని ప్రాముఖ్యతను వివరించండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Interpret Ashoka's Rock Edict XII on inter-faith harmony and secularism.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: List the historical literary sources that help us reconstruct Mauryan history and specify the author and subject of each work.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: మౌర్యుల చరిత్రను తెలుసుకోవడానికి ఉపయోగపడే చారిత్రక గ్రంథాలు, వాటి రచయితలు, గ్రంథ విషయాలను పట్టిక రూపంలో రాయండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Tabulate Mauryan historical sources: Arthashastra, Indica, Deepavamsa, Mudrarakshasa.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, locate major Ashokan inscription sites: (a) Sarnath, (b) Kalinga (Dhauli), (c) Pataliputra, (d) Taxila, (e) Yerragudi (Andhra Pradesh).
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో అశోకుని ప్రధాన శాసన ప్రదేశాలను గుర్తించండి: (a) సారనాథ్, (b) కళింగ (ధౌళి), (c) పాటలీపుత్ర, (d) తక్షశిల, (e) ఎర్రగుడి (ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్).
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Locate Ashokan rock and pillar edict sites on map of India.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: How do you appreciate the design of the Sarnath Lion Capital which has been adopted as the National Emblem of Independent India?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారత జాతీయ చిహ్నంగా స్వీకరించబడిన సారనాథ్ సింహ రాజధాని (సింహ శిఖరం) యొక్క శిల్పకళా సౌందర్యాన్ని, నైతిక సందేశాన్ని మీరు ఎలా అభినందిస్తారు?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Appreciate architectural majesty and democratic symbolism of Sarnath Lion Capital.

core_themes: What is government? Need for rules, laws, public order, and collective decision making.
Key functions of government: maintaining law and order, protecting boundaries, ensuring welfare, building infrastructure, managing disasters.
Three levels of government in India: Local level (village/town), State level (Andhra Pradesh), National/Central level (India).
Three organs of government: Legislature (makes laws), Executive (implements laws), Judiciary (resolves disputes and interprets laws).
Types of government: Monarchy, Dictatorship, and Democracy (Representative Democracy).
Universal Adult Suffrage (right to vote for all adult citizens aged 18 and above without discrimination).
Women's Suffrage Movement (struggle for voting rights in UK and USA).
learning_outcomes: Define government and identify its primary functions in citizen welfare.
Differentiate between the three levels of government: local, state, and central.
Explain the significance of Universal Adult Suffrage and free and fair elections.
Contrast democracy with monarchy and dictatorship.
summary_points: A government is an institution through which a society makes and enforces public policies.
India is a representative democracy where citizens elect leaders to make decisions on their behalf.
Universal Adult Suffrage means that all citizens aged 18 and above have one vote with equal value.
Laws made by the legislature must be obeyed by everyone; courts ensure laws are followed.
map_skills: Map of India showing States and Union Territories

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What do you understand by the word 'government'? List five ways in which the government affects your daily life.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 'ప్రభుత్వం' అంటే మీరు ఏమి అర్థం చేసుకున్నారు? మీ దైనందిన జీవితంపై ప్రభుత్వం చూపే ఐదు ప్రభావాలను పేర్కొనండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Define government and list five daily civic touchpoints.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Differentiate between a Democratic government and a Monarchy.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ప్రజాస్వామ్య ప్రభుత్వానికి మరియు రాచరిక ప్రభుత్వానికి మధ్య గల తేడాలను వివరించండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Distinguish between democracy and monarchy.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read the section on 'Women's Suffrage Movement' and explain why women had to struggle to get the right to vote in Western democracies.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 'మహిళా ఓటుహక్కు ఉద్యమం' భాగాన్ని చదివి, పాశ్చాత్య దేశాలలో మహిళలు ఓటుహక్కు సాధించడానికి ఎందుకు పోరాడాల్సి వచ్చిందో వివరించండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Interpret historical struggle for women's suffrage in UK and USA.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Classify the following government decisions into Local, State, or Central level: (a) Construction of village road in Chittoor, (b) Introduction of new 500-rupee currency note, (c) Decision to hold Class 10 board exams in AP, (d) Signing peace treaty with neighboring country.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: క్రింది ప్రభుత్వ నిర్ణయాలను స్థానిక, రాష్ట్ర లేదా కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వ స్థాయిలుగా వర్గీకరించండి: (a) చిత్తూరులోని ఒక గ్రామీణ రహదారి నిర్మాణం, (b) కొత్త 500 రూపాయల నోటు విడుదల, (c) ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ లో పదవ తరగతి పరీక్షల నిర్వహణ, (d) పొరుగు దేశంతో శాంతి ఒప్పందం కుదుర్చుకోవడం.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Classify government decisions into local, state, and central levels.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why is Universal Adult Suffrage considered the cornerstone of Indian democracy? What would happen if voting rights were restricted only to educated or wealthy citizens?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: సార్వత్రిక వయోజన ఓటుహక్కును భారత ప్రజాస్వామ్యానికి పునాదిగా ఎందుకు భావిస్తారు? కేవలం చదువుకున్నవారికి లేదా ధనవంతులకే ఓటుహక్కు పరిమితం చేస్తే ఏమవుతుంది?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Reflect on democratic equality through Universal Adult Suffrage.

core_themes: Decentralization of power and local democracy in rural and urban areas.
Panchayati Raj System (Three-tier structure): Gram Panchayat at village level, Mandal Parishad at mandal level, Zilla Parishad at district level.
Gram Sabha: General body meeting of all adult registered voters in a village, role in approving plans and monitoring Sarpanch.
Gram Panchayat: Wards, Ward Members (Ward Councillors), Sarpanch (elected head), and Panchayat Secretary (appointed government official).
Functions of Gram Panchayat: Water supply, drainage, rural roads, street lighting, sanitation, maintaining village records.
Urban Local Bodies: Nagar Panchayat (transitional town), Municipality (medium town), Municipal Corporation (large city with Mayor and Municipal Commissioner).
Sources of revenue for local bodies: House tax, water tax, property tax, stamp duty, state government grants.
learning_outcomes: Explain the structure and functioning of Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat.
Describe the three-tier Panchayati Raj system in Andhra Pradesh.
Differentiate between rural local bodies (Panchayats) and urban local bodies (Municipalities / Corporations).
Appreciate the importance of citizen participation in local governance.
summary_points: Gram Sabha is the supreme democratic body in a village where all adult residents can participate and question officials.
Every village Panchayat is divided into wards, each represented by an elected Ward Member.
Panchayat Secretary records minutes of meetings and oversees implementation of government development schemes.
In large cities like Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada, municipal administration is headed by a Municipal Commissioner.
map_skills: District and Mandal administrative boundaries map of Andhra Pradesh

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is the relation between a Gram Sabha and a Gram Panchayat? Who can be a member of the Gram Sabha?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: గ్రామసభ మరియు గ్రామ పంచాయతీల మధ్య సంబంధం ఏమిటి? గ్రామసభలో ఎవరు సభ్యులుగా ఉంటారు?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Explain relationship between Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What are the key civic functions performed by a Municipal Corporation in an urban area?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: పట్టణ ప్రాంతాలలో నగరపాలక సంస్థ (మున్సిపల్ కార్పొరేషన్) నిర్వహించే ముఖ్యమైన పౌర విధులు ఏమిటి?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Describe civic duties of Municipal Corporations in urban cities.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Draw an organizational flowchart showing the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure from village to district level in Andhra Pradesh.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ లో గ్రామ స్థాయి నుండి జిల్లా స్థాయి వరకు గల మూడంచెల పంచాయతీరాజ్ వ్యవస్థను చూపే ఫ్లోచార్ట్‌ను గీయండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Create flowchart of three-tier Panchayati Raj administration.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why is regular attendance of villagers in Gram Sabha meetings crucial for eliminating corruption in village development projects?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: గ్రామ అభివృద్ధి పనులలో అవినీతిని అరికట్టడానికి గ్రామస్తులు క్రమం తప్పకుండా గ్రామసభలకు హాజరుకావడం ఎందుకు చాలా అవసరం?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Reflect on citizen vigilance in Gram Sabha for transparent governance.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Appreciate the hard work done by municipal sanitary sanitation workers who clean drains and roads every day to keep our towns disease-free.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: మన ఊర్లు, పట్టణాలు రోగాల బారిన పడకుండా ప్రతిరోజూ వీధులను, మురుగు కాలువలను శుభ్రపరిచే పారిశుధ్య కార్మికుల సేవలను మీరు ఎలా అభినందిస్తారు?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Express gratitude and empathy towards municipal sanitation workers.

core_themes: Cultural richness and diversity of India: Unity in Diversity.
Languages of India: Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic, and Tibeto-Burman language families; 22 Scheduled languages.
Classical languages of India (Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia).
Major religions born in India: Hinduism (Vedic wisdom, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, Epics: Ramayana and Mahabharata).
Buddhism: Gautama Buddha, teachings of Four Noble Truths and Eightfold Path (Ashtangika Marga), spread to Sri Lanka, China, Southeast Asia.
Jainism: Vardhamana Mahavira, principles of Ahimsa (non-injury), Satya, Asteya, Brahmacharya, Aparigraha; Triratnas.
World religions in India: Islam, Christianity, Sikhism, Zoroastrianism, and Judaism.
Ancient art, sculpture, and cave architecture: Amaravati Stupa, Nagarjunakonda, Ajanta and Ellora caves.
learning_outcomes: Recognize the linguistic diversity and major language families in India.
Explain the core ethical teachings of Buddhism and Jainism.
Appreciate the artistic brilliance of ancient Buddhist stupas like Amaravati in Andhra Pradesh.
Embrace religious tolerance and pluralistic cultural values.
summary_points: India's culture is a synthesis of diverse customs, faiths, arts, and languages evolving over millennia.
Telugu is recognized as a classical language known for its rich literary tradition and sweetness ('Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa').
Gautama Buddha preached Dhamma in simple Prakrit so common people could easily understand.
Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda in Andhra Pradesh were world-renowned centers of Mahayana Buddhism and art.
map_skills: Ancient cultural and religious heritage sites: Sanchi, Amaravati, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Sravanabelagola

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What were the main teachings of Gautama Buddha? Name the Four Noble Truths.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: గౌతమ బుద్ధుని ప్రధాన బోధనలు ఏవి? చతురార్య సత్యాలను పేర్కొనండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: State Buddha's Four Noble Truths and Eightfold Path.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What are the Three Jewels (Triratnas) of Jainism taught by Lord Mahavira?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: వర్ధమాన మహావీరుడు బోధించిన జైనమత త్రిరత్నాలు ఏవి?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: State the Three Jewels (Triratnas) of Jainism.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read the section on 'The Stupa of Amaravati' and explain how Buddhist art depicted life stories of the Buddha (Jataka tales) in limestone relief sculptures.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 'అమరావతి స్తూపం' భాగాన్ని చదివి, బౌద్ధ శిల్పులు సున్నపురాతి పలకలపై బుద్ధుని జీవిత ఘట్టాలను (జాతక కథలు) ఏ విధంగా మలిచారో వివరించండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Interpret the narrative Buddhist art on limestone relief panels at Amaravati.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Classify the major classical languages of India into their respective linguistic families: (a) Sanskrit, (b) Tamil, (c) Telugu, (d) Kannada, (e) Malayalam, (f) Odia.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతీయ ప్రాచీన (క్లాసికల్) భాషలను వాటి భాషా కుటుంబాల ఆధారంగా వర్గీకరించండి: (a) సంస్కృతం, (b) తమిళం, (c) తెలుగు, (d) కన్నడ, (e) మలయాళం, (f) ఒడియా.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Classify classical Indian languages into Indo-Aryan and Dravidian language families.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, locate and label: (a) Bodh Gaya, (b) Sanchi, (c) Amaravati, (d) Nagarjunakonda, (e) Sravanabelagola.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో గుర్తించండి: (a) బోధగయ, (b) సాంచి, (c) అమరావతి, (d) నాగార్జునకొండ, (e) శ్రవణబెళగొళ.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Locate major Buddhist and Jain cultural centers on India map.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: How does the principle of 'Unity in Diversity' define the essence of Indian society? Express your appreciation with examples from festivals celebrated in Andhra Pradesh.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 'భిన్నత్వంలో ఏకత్వం' అనే సూత్రం భారతీయ సమాజ ఔన్నత్యాన్ని ఎలా ప్రతిబింబిస్తుంది? ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ లో జరుపుకునే పండుగల ఉదాహరణలతో మీ భావనను వ్యక్తం చేయండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Express appreciation for Unity in Diversity with festivals of Andhra Pradesh.

core_themes: Diversity vs Discrimination: Differences turn into discrimination when people act on prejudices and stereotypes.
Prejudice (judging other people negatively) and Stereotypes (fixing people into rigid mental images).
Gender stereotyping ('Boys don't cry', 'Girls should only do domestic work') and its harmful social impacts.
Caste-based discrimination, social inequality, and untouchability in historical India.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar: Childhood experience of discrimination at Koregaon, struggle for social justice, drafting the Constitution of India as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.
Constitutional safeguards for equality: Fundamental Right to Equality (Articles 14–18), abolition of untouchability (Article 17), freedom to pursue any profession, secularism.
Government affirmative initiatives: Mid-day Meal Scheme, reservation policies, welfare schemes for women and disadvantaged sections.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between difference, prejudice, stereotype, and discrimination.
Recognize gender stereotypes and challenge discriminatory societal norms.
Explain the constitutional ideals and laws framed to ensure equality for all citizens.
Appreciate the visionary leadership and struggles of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in building an egalitarian India.
summary_points: Prejudice means to judge others negatively or look down upon them.
A stereotype creates a fixed, rigid image of a group, ignoring individual abilities and uniqueness.
The Indian Constitution guarantees that all people of India are equal before the law, regardless of religion, caste, sex, or economic status.
Untouchability is legally abolished and its practice in any form is a punishable crime by law.
map_skills: Birthplace and key historical struggle centers of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in India

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is the difference between prejudice and stereotype? Give one example of each.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రక్షక భావన (పక్షపాతం) మరియు మూసధోరణి (స్టీరియోటైప్) ల మధ్య గల తేడా ఏమిటి? ఒక్కొక్క ఉదాహరణ ఇవ్వండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Distinguish between prejudice and stereotype with everyday examples.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What provisions are made in the Constitution of India to ensure equality for all citizens?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: పౌరులందరికీ సమానత్వాన్ని కల్పించడానికి భారత రాజ్యాంగంలో ఏ నిబంధనలను చేర్చారు?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Explain constitutional provisions ensuring equality for all citizens.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's childhood experience at Koregaon railway station and interpret how untouchability denied human dignity to innocent children.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: కొరేగావ్ రైల్వే స్టేషన్ వద్ద డా. బి.ఆర్. అంబేద్కర్ బాల్య అనుభవాన్ని చదివి, అంటరానితనం అమాయక పిల్లల ఆత్మగౌరవాన్ని ఏ విధంగా దెబ్బతీసిందో వివరించండి.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Interpret Ambedkar's Koregaon experience on the cruelty of untouchability.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: How does the Mid-Day Meal scheme implemented in government schools promote social equality among children of different castes?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ప్రభుత్వ పాఠశాలల్లో అమలుచేస్తున్న మధ్యాహ్న భోజన పథకం వివిధ కులాల పిల్లల మధ్య సామాజిక సమానత్వాన్ని ఎలా పెంపొందిస్తుంది?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Reflect on how Mid-Day Meal scheme breaks caste and gender barriers.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: How do you appreciate the tireless contribution of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in framing the Constitution of India and championing the rights of oppressed communities?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారత రాజ్యాంగ రూపకల్పనలో మరియు అణగారిన వర్గాల హక్కుల పరిరక్షణలో డా. బి.ఆర్. అంబేద్కర్ చేసిన విశేష కృషిని మీరు ఎలా అభినందిస్తారు?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text: Express appreciation for Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's crusade for human dignity and constitutional equality.
